result.title: Counterfactual Model Testing Under Distribution Shift
result.summary: Deployed machine learning (ML) models can degrade as the distribution of their input data shifts. Such shifts can result from changes in the population or from data integrity issues in the pipeline that materializes model features, two sources that operate through different mechanisms. Because labels are often absent or delayed, it is common practice to track shifts in the data instead, but a detected shift does not indicate how it affects the model. We formulate this problem as online model testing under distribution shift. Testing requires reproducing the shift on a controlled baseline with known labels. Since the same shift can come from either source, doing so requires knowing which mechanism changed. We propose a methodology that reproduces observed changes in both mechanisms to estimate current performance and the potential gain from repairing observed data integrity issues. Experiments on real-world datasets with simulated faults show that separating the two sources generally improves both estimates, supporting this formulation. A churn prediction case illustrates how these tests can support monitoring and repair prioritization

AI.brief_summary: 论文将分布漂移下部署模型的性能退化问题表述为「在线模型测试」，提出在标签已知的受控基线上分别复现总体变化与特征管线的数据完整性故障这两种机制，以估计当前性能及修复数据问题可能带来的收益，并在真实数据集的模拟故障与流失预测案例中验证该分解通常能改善两类估计。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「分机制反事实复现 + 已知标签受控基线」的评估思路，可能为 LVR 中区分视觉证据、latent 状态与训练轨迹各自贡献、以及在标签缺失时评估答案对 latent 内容的实际使用程度提供借鉴线索，但领域相距较远，需核查可迁移性。
